subject: Post-demo quick recap + ask: targeted regression criteria & pin next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@clearbanking.com>
Cc: Sophie Liu <sophie.liu@clearbanking.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo quick recap + ask: targeted regression criteria & pin next steps

Hi Alex / Sophie —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and the concrete asks we promised:

- Summary: ClearBanking demo looked great; primary risk area you flagged was the customer-address normalization path where a small set of examples produced wrong substitutions after our recent model refresh.
- Recommended working set: for your use case we think the stability sweet spot is the small-latency variant we discussed (rwd-small-1.2) for now, with the higher-capacity rwd-medium-1.3 reserved for higher-throughput batches once we validate.
- Artifacts attached: prompt_set_v1 (a curated 60-case golden prompt set), and a short benchmark dashboard link below.

Immediate asks from you:
1) Can you drop 8–12 representative prompts (real examples, redacted PII ok) into the reply below or share a Drive folder? Those will be used for a focused regression run.
2) Confirm any SLAs around token-latency or throughput we should preserve during rollback/pinning.

Planned next steps on our side:
- Rishi/Monica will run a narrow diff between the v1.2 and v1.3 variants against your supplied prompts and push a short snapshot report within 24 hours.
- If diffs exceed the thresholds we agree on, we will open an internal pin request and outline a rollback checklist.

Benchmarks & assets: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/clearbanking/2027-06
Attached: soojin_eval_pack_prompt_set_v1.json

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute triage tomorrow afternoon to walk through the examples.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@clearbanking.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Liu <sophie.liu@clearbanking.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo quick recap + ask: targeted regression criteria & pin next steps

Thanks Soojin — appreciated.

Quick answers:
- I attached a short CSV with 10 redacted prompts we've seen failure modes on (column: prompt_id, prompt_text, observed_issue). The two most concerning failures are incorrect entity merges and a few hallucinated bank routing tags.
- SLA/constraints: we need per-request p95 latency to stay below 180ms for single-shot address-normalization calls. Throughput is less critical for this first pass.

I'm worried because we did see a sharp degradation after your team pushed updates last Thursday — some outputs look subtly different (tokenization differences suspected). Can you confirm whether a rollback/pinning option exists if the targeted diff run shows regressions? We'd need a plan that doesn't disrupt our signed pilot.

If helpful, here's one example inline: 

> prompt_id: cb-07
> prompt: "Normalize address: 10A Baker St., Apt #4B, London"
> observed: "10 A Baker Street Apt 4B London" (expected: 10A Baker St -> 10A Baker St.) — small punctuation/formatting regressions that break downstream regexes.

Happy to hop on a call today 4pm BST if that's easier.

Best,
Alex Turner
Product Lead, ClearBanking
alex.turner@clearbanking.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@clearbanking.com>, Sophie Liu <sophie.liu@clearbanking.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo quick recap + ask: targeted regression criteria & pin next steps

Thanks Alex — good signal, and timely. High-level from infra/model engineering:

- What changed: last Thursday we promoted a tokenization micro-tweak in the sequence-preprocessor and shipped a medium-capacity variant (rwd-medium-1.3) that uses a slightly different subword merge heuristic. That change reduced token counts for long-form prompts (good for cost) but can alter punctuation adjacency in edge cases — exactly what's showing up in your cb-07 example.

- Short-term mitigation options (ranked):
  1) Pin ClearBanking pilot to rwd-small-1.2 immediately (fastest, non-invasive). We can do an internal pin that routes your API key to v1.2 within our routing layer.
  2) Apply a prompt normalization shim on our side: a lightweight post-process patch that enforces your address formatting rules (medium work, lower-resilience than pin).
  3) Full rollback of medium variant (only if pin + shim insufficient). This is heavier—requires infra ops to recompose the pool and validate smoke tests.

Attached is a quick snapshot we ran against Soojin's golden prompt_set_v1: eval_snapshot_v1.2_vs_v1.3.csv. The diff column highlights where outputs diverge on normalized tokens and a simple BLEU-style scoring. You'll see most cases are stable, but the address family has the highest divergence.

Next actions I'm proposing:
- Soojin: confirm you received Alex's CSV with the 10 prompts.
- Alex: if you can confirm 3–5 high-priority prompts from that CSV, Rishi will run the pin + targeted regression and produce a short decision memo.
- Monica: please prepare the pin_request_form.pdf and the internal rollback_playbook.md so we can move quickly if thresholds are exceeded.

I'll own the targeted diff run and the decision memo; aim to share within 18 hours.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@clearbanking.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo quick recap + ask: targeted regression criteria & pin next steps

Alex — thanks for the CSV and the example. Confirmed next steps and timeline:

1) I've uploaded your CSV to our secure evaluation folder and shared it with the team.
2) Rishi will run the targeted diff against the 10 prompts and the attached golden set; expect a one-page memo plus the CSV snapshot within 18 hours.
3) If the memo flags >2 high-severity regressions (where high-severity = incorrect entity transforms or anything that breaks token-level downstream regexes), we will open a pin_request_form and apply routing to lock your key to rwd-small-1.2. That pin will be staged and validated in the staging pool before flipping live; expected user-visible window for the pin is ~30 minutes once approved.
4) Monica will prepare the pin_request_form.pdf and the rollback_playbook.md; I attached the eval pack I sent earlier for reference.

Can you confirm the 3–5 highest priority prompt_ids to prioritize? If we don't hear back by EOB your local time, we'll proceed to prioritize cb-07, cb-02, cb-09.

If this sounds good, I'll schedule a 30-minute triage for tomorrow at 4pm BST and include an Ops owner in case we need a rapid pin.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

(Attachments: soojin_eval_pack_prompt_set_v1.json, pin_request_form.pdf, rishi_rollback_playbook.md, eval_snapshot_v1.2_vs_v1.3.csv)
